{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mn-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"3578ccbded7a74268c2a45695baa964b8c60bf1a11bbe8bac41257557ccce042","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mn-class-d:lineage:85","source_registry_sha256":"960e2daa314aff60b32f5124e42324d79615ce2a3ea953a336216b4593c0c910","source_liveness_sha256":"0b70283fc58b1f8ea1822994a92e3ce7ff4b722004376a9cd819180969b6fe1e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Getting a Minnesota license: eligibility, documents and the three tests","heading":"C — Your license to drive, part one: who needs a license, who cannot be licensed, identification and documents, the written test, the vision screening and the road test","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Your license to drive, part one: who needs a license, who cannot be licensed, identification and documents, the written test, the vision screening and the road test
Knowledge domain: the path from no license to a Minnesota Class D license — who must hold one and who is exempt, what stops a license from being issued, the identity and residency documents, and how the written test, vision screening and road test are run and scored.

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
Driving on Minnesota public streets or highways requires a driver's license that is valid and not expired. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
Someone who has never held a license anywhere must pass a written test and a vision test, get an instruction permit and then pass a road test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
A Minnesota license that expired more than one year but less than five years ago means you must pass both the vision test and the written test, and only then apply for a new license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
A new resident aged 21 or older from another state, certain U.S. territories or Canada who shows a valid, unexpired license gets a Minnesota license with only a vision test and an application, and no written or road test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
For that new resident, a former license expired less than one year means passing the written test, and one expired more than one year means passing both the written and road tests. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
A new Minnesota resident has 60 days to get a Minnesota license or permit, while a commercial driver has 30 days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
A newcomer from a country other than the U.S. or Canada must pass the written, vision and road tests even with a valid license from the former country. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
You cannot obtain your Minnesota driver's license until you present every other driver's license and identification card you hold to DVS [A01].
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
A nonresident at least 15 years old with a valid license from the home state or country may drive in Minnesota without a Minnesota license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
A nonresident at least 18 years old from a country that does not license drivers may drive a vehicle registered there for the current year in Minnesota for up to 90 days in a calendar year without a license or permit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A02
You cannot be licensed if you fail to show proper identification, fail any required test, or cannot read and understand official road signs or state traffic laws. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A02
No license or instruction permit is issued to anyone under 15 years of age. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
An applicant under 18 without a valid license from another state cannot be licensed unless they present proof of completing an approved driver education course. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
A license is refused to an applicant 18 or younger who has held an instruction permit for under six months, and to one 19 or older who has held it for under three months. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
A suspended or revoked license blocks a new license until every reinstatement requirement is met, and a canceled license also blocks issuance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
The Commissioner of Public Safety may refuse a license for a physical or mental disability that prevents safe driving or for good cause to believe your driving would harm public safety, and a court finding of mental incompetence can also block it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A02
For the written and road tests your identification must verify your first, middle and last name and your date of birth, and mismatched names require certified proof of each legal name change. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A02
DVS may refuse laminated or altered documents, never accepts photocopies of identification, and may confiscate fraudulent documents. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A03
For a standard license or ID you may show a Minnesota license, ID or permit that is current or expired no more than five years if it has a photo, or no more than one year if it has none. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A03
Without such a card you present two documents, a primary and a secondary, and one of them must show your full name and date of birth. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A03
Under the Driver's License for All law, since Oct. 1, 2023 a standard license, learner's permit or state ID can be issued regardless of immigration status, without proof of legal presence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A03
A REAL ID compliant card needs one document proving identity, date of birth and legal presence, knowledge of your Social Security number, and two documents proving current Minnesota residency, all presented in person. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A04
You must give your Social Security number on the DVS application or check the box saying none was issued; the number is never printed on or embedded in the card, and an eligible applicant who withholds it cannot be processed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A05
The Class D written test is given at DVS exam stations by appointment and uses multiple choice and true-or-false questions on Minnesota traffic laws and road signs, on paper or on a computer. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A05
Computer test stations offer the written test in English, several other languages or American Sign Language, and headphones let you hear the questions while you read. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A05
You may take only one written test per day, and you need a score of 80 percent to pass. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A05
Two consecutive failed written tests trigger a $10 fee for the third attempt and every attempt after it. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A05
Classroom driver education is not required for written-test applicants who are 18 or older, while those under 18 show a Blue Card or Pink Card certificate of enrollment. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A05
The vision screening requires normal or corrected vision of at least 20/40 and peripheral vision of at least 105 degrees. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A05
Failing the vision screening or having peripheral vision below 105 degrees sends you to an eye doctor, whose report to the DVS Driver Evaluation Unit decides whether you may drive or need correction or restrictions. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A05
The road test has three parts: showing the vehicle's safety equipment, showing vehicle control skills, and a driving test in normal traffic, and you will never be asked to do anything illegal. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A05
For the road test you bring a valid instruction permit and current proof of insurance and your own vehicle; a neighborhood electric vehicle is not allowed, and a rental vehicle must list you as a driver. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A05
A backup camera may be used on the road test, but it must not be your only way of checking behind the vehicle while backing. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A06
During the road test there is no smoking, no phone or electronic device use, no passengers of any kind including pets, children or interpreters, and parking assist may not be used for parallel parking. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A06
The safety equipment check can cover the seat, seat belts, parking brake, high and low beams, hazard flashers, horn, wipers, defroster and fan, mirrors and fuel gauge, and failing it ends your road test for that day. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A07
Road test scoring covers vehicle control, parallel parking, parking on a hill, turns and signals, lane use, response to signs and conditions, attention to pedestrians, and a 90-degree backing maneuver into a space 10 feet wide. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A07
You fail the road test immediately for breaking a traffic law, driving dangerously or recklessly, needing the examiner's help to control the vehicle, an avoidable crash even when not legally at fault, or refusing the examiner's instructions. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A07
After two failed road tests each further attempt costs a $20 retest fee, and after four failures you need a minimum of six hours of behind-the-wheel training from a licensed instructor before testing again. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A07
A failed road test comes with assigned practice time that must be finished before the next attempt. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A07
A permit or license holder newly diagnosed with epilepsy or another condition that can cause loss of consciousness must send a physician's statement to DVS within 30 days of the diagnosis. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0015]

Misconceptions: a new resident does not automatically skip every test, because the age, the license status and the expiry age of the old license decide which tests apply; a backup camera is allowed but cannot replace looking back; passengers and interpreters are never allowed on the road test; an avoidable crash fails the road test even when the other driver is legally at fault.
Mnemonics: twenty-forty and one-oh-five for the eyes; one written test a day, eighty to pass; road test parts are equipment, control, drive.
Glossary: instruction permit means the learner permit held before the road test; enhanced license means the citizenship-based card that lists a Minnesota address; REAL ID means the federally compliant card needing legal presence and residency proof; Driver Evaluation Unit means the DVS office that reviews vision and medical reports; reintegration license means the temporary license for people released from prison.
Dynamic facts: fees, appointment websites, phone numbers, the language list and document rules change over time; confirm them at drive.mn.gov and the DVS document pages.
